part_title: Model Dashboard and Production Model Monitoring

scenes.title: SageMaker – Model Dashboard
scenes.narration: Read the main row from left to right. SageMaker Model Dashboard brings together the model inventory, which shows deployed model details and status; model cards, which document intended use and evaluation evidence; monitoring alerts; and quality and bias insights. The purple dashboard panel collects those signals so an operator can investigate rather than search several disconnected screens. In the bottom example a data-drift alert has been triggered. The dashboard highlights that alert and displays a trend chart, and the operator then checks the alert details, reviews the model card, and inspects quality and bias metrics before choosing a response. Possible actions include checking the source data or considering retraining, but an alert alone does not prove retraining is necessary. The exam distinction is between this central investigation view and Model Monitor, which runs the actual monitoring checks. A dashboard helps the team understand and act on evidence; it does not automatically guarantee a safe or accurate model.

scenes.title: SageMaker – Model Monitor
scenes.narration: Follow all six numbered steps across the slide. A SageMaker endpoint captures production inputs and model predictions. The captured inference data is stored in Amazon S3 and compared with a baseline, which is a reference distribution from training or a previous period. SageMaker Model Monitor performs scheduled checks for data-quality problems and statistical drift. Drift means that feature or prediction patterns have changed from that baseline; it does not automatically mean the model is wrong. If configured thresholds are crossed, Amazon CloudWatch can raise an alert. A person investigates the reports and, only if justified, decides to retrain and deploy a new version. The lower e-commerce example starts with a product recommender, notices changed customer behavior, and shows that investigation before retraining. The important contrast is that Model Monitor detects and reports issues, CloudWatch delivers alerting, and people or configured workflows decide how to remediate them. Model quality monitoring may also need ground-truth labels that arrive after predictions.
